Item: Social Security wage base and benefit bend points
How often: Yearly. Switch with the federal tax figures on January 1
Source: SSA's annual COLA and wage-base fact sheet, released in October
What it is: The Social Security tax wage cap (also the cap on earnings the benefit estimate counts) and the two bend points in the benefit formula.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/math.js: FICA.ssCap, SS_CAP, SS_BEND1, SS_BEND2

How often: Monthly
Source: multpl.com Shiller PE (monthly)
What it is: The latest Shiller CAPE, shown against the historical record and used by the CAPE withdrawal strategy's 'today' figures.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/math.js: CAPE_NOW, CAPE_NOW_ASOF

How often: Yearly, after College Board publishes
Source: College Board, Trends in College Pricing (published in late October)
What it is: The yearly cost of a public in-state and a private school (tuition, room and board) the College Savings tool offers.
Where in the code: web/tools/college/model.ts: the presets and default kid; web/content/articles/college.html: the worked example

Item: Federal income tax brackets and deductions
How often: Yearly. Prepare in November or December; switch on January 1
Source: IRS revenue procedure for the coming tax year (Rev. Proc. 2025-32 gave 2026), usually out in late October
What it is: Federal brackets, standard deduction, long-term capital gains breakpoints, the age-65 extra standard deduction, and the 2025-2028 senior deduction.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/math.js: FED_2026, FED_STD, LTCG_2026, SENIOR_ADDL, SENIOR_BONUS

Item: Medicare Part B premium and IRMAA tiers
How often: Yearly. Switch on January 1
Source: CMS Medicare Parts A and B premiums and deductibles fact sheet, usually out in October or November
What it is: The standard Part B premium and the income tiers that raise Part B and Part D for higher earners.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/math.js: IRMAA (the Healthcare tool reads it through HC_IRMAA)

Item: Medicare Part D and Medigap cost estimates
How often: Yearly, in the fall
Source: CMS Part D premium announcement (summer); KFF or insurer surveys for Medigap
What it is: The average standalone Part D premium and the rough monthly range for a Medigap Plan G policy at 65.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/plan.js: PL_MED_PARTD; web/tools/healthcare/model.ts: HC_PARTD_BASE, HC_MEDIGAP_LOW, HC_MEDIGAP_HIGH

How often: Yearly, for the coming coverage year
Source: KFF Marketplace Average Benchmark Premiums (late October or November); HHS poverty guidelines (January, used for the next coverage year); IRS applicable-percentage revenue procedure (summer)
What it is: Average benchmark Silver premium by state, the poverty line the subsidies are measured against, the subsidy percentages, and whether the enhanced credits are back.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/math.js: HC_FPL_BASE, HC_FPL_PER_ADDL, HC_STATE_PREMIUM_40, the applicable-percentage table below them; web/tools/healthcare/Healthcare.tsx and web/tools/about/About.tsx: the '2026 ACA rules' text

How often: Yearly check. The tables rarely change (last in 2022), but rmdStartAge's year must roll every January
Source: IRS Publication 590-B
What it is: The IRS Uniform Lifetime Table (RMDs), the Single Life table (72(t) payments), and the RMD starting age, which works out birth year from a hard-coded 2026.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/math.js: ULT, rmdStartAge (the 2026 in it); web/lib/engine/bridge.js: BR_SLT

Item: The tax year named in the site's text
How often: Yearly, on January 1, together with the federal switch
Source: Follows the tax items above
What it is: Every place the site says '2026' about its rules: page titles and descriptions, tool badges and headings, the footer, preview cards, articles and FAQs.
Where in the code: web/lib/page-meta.json; web/lib/cards.ts; web/components/shell/Footer.tsx; web/content/articles/*.html; web/tools/**: 'grep -rn 2026 web --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx'

How often: Each article every 90 days (set max_age_days to change it)
Source: The article's own sources and the site's current figures
What it is: Each tool page's article shows the month it was last reviewed. A review means checking its figures, sources and links still hold; only then move its date.
Where in the code: web/content/articles/*.html: data-reviewed on each <article>

How often: Quarterly check; only matters if 120% of the mid-term rate goes above 5%
Source: IRS Applicable Federal Rates (monthly revenue rulings)
What it is: The rate the Bridge's 72(t) payment starts with: up to the greater of 5% or 120% of the federal mid-term rate.
Where in the code: web/tools/bridge/model.ts: seppRate

How often: Quarterly, or sooner if rates move more than half a point
Source: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey (weekly); use a rounded recent average
What it is: The 30-year rate the Mortgage and Rent vs. Buy tools start with. The pages call it a starting point, not a live quote.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/math.js: MORT_RATE_30 (and its comment)

Item: New laws that change the rules mid-year
How often: Quarterly check
Source: IRS newsroom, Tax Foundation tracker, KFF for ACA, state revenue departments
What it is: Federal or state legislation that changes brackets, deductions, ACA subsidies (the enhanced credits that expired after 2025), RMD ages or Social Security taxation between the yearly updates.
Where in the code: Wherever the law lands; usually web/lib/engine/math.js and the articles

How often: Yearly: add the past year's 12 months once December's data is in
Source: Robert Shiller's dataset (Yale), via multpl, for prices, dividends, yields and CAPE; US BLS for CPI-U (December's CPI comes out mid-January)
What it is: Monthly S&P 500 total returns, 10-year Treasury returns, CPI-U inflation and the historical CAPE series, January 1926 onward. Every historical test on the site runs on these.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/math.js: HIST_M_STOCK, HIST_M_BOND, HIST_M_INFL, HIST_M_CAPE (and the '1,200 months' comment); web/components/shell/Footer.tsx and the articles: '1926 to 2025'

Item: State income tax brackets and deductions (50 states and DC)
How often: Yearly, after the Tax Foundation survey comes out
Source: Tax Foundation, State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets (as of January 1), usually published in February; state revenue departments for detail
What it is: Every state's brackets, standard deduction, personal exemption and credits. Illinois has extra detail (exemption cliff, 65+ amount).
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/math.js: STATES

How often: Yearly, with the market history, once French posts December
Source: Kenneth R. French Data Library (Dartmouth): the Fama-French factors file for T-bills, the 2x3 size/book-to-market portfolios for small value
What it is: Monthly one-month Treasury bill and small-company value returns, July 1926 onward.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/math.js: HIST_M_CASH, HIST_M_SV

How often: Yearly, early in the year
Source: State revenue departments; Tax Foundation and AARP state guides as a cross-check
What it is: Which states tax Social Security, pension and IRA exclusions, extra deductions or credits at 65, and states with no early-withdrawal penalty add-on.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/math.js: RET_STATE, SS_TAX_STATES; web/lib/engine/plan.js: PL_NOEXP (also used by the Bridge)

Item: Home price, rent and housing-cost defaults
How often: Yearly
Source: NAR or Census median home price; Census or Zillow median rent; Tax Foundation property tax rates
What it is: The starting home price, rent, rent growth, home appreciation, property tax rate and insurance in the Mortgage and Rent vs. Buy tools.
Where in the code: web/tools/mortgage/model.ts: MORTGAGE_DEFAULTS; web/tools/rentbuy/model.ts: RENTBUY_DEFAULTS

How often: Yearly
Source: Federal Reserve G.19 consumer credit report (credit card rates)
What it is: The example debts' interest rates, mainly the credit card APR.
Where in the code: web/tools/debt/model.ts: ROWS; web/content/articles/debt.html (if it quotes them)

How often: Yearly review; change rarely
Source: Long-run history on the site itself; Vanguard and Morningstar capital-market outlooks as a sanity check
What it is: Default return before inflation (8.5%), inflation (3%), college cost growth (4%), heirs' tax rate and similar starting assumptions.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/calculators.js: DEFAULTS, BASIC_DEFAULTS, RISK_LEVELS; web/tools/*/model.ts: each tool's defaults; web/lib/engine/plan.js: PL_HEIR
